newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline softens with crude in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline softens with crude in thin trade.

text.p: NWE gasoline was thinly traded on Friday and prices were $2 or so weaker.
Eurograde barges traded between $218-219 fob AR, but activity was variously described as "flat".
Gasoline cargoes were also easier with pressure coming from weaker NYMEX gasoline which was down 70 points or so at 67.70 cents a gallon in the late afternoon.
The softer tone surrounding crude gave no support.
Good supplies of gasoline in Europe resulting from local refineries pumping out mogas in the drive for middle distillates production also added to the bearish tone.

With only muted NWE demand several dealers thought European gasoline would have to shed some weight in order to conclusively re-open the arbitrage opportunity, which was viewed as shut from the Rotterdam region.
Some interest into Lebanon for 10-20,000 tonnes for promptish delivery was seen in the Med.
